answer.reason: The after source supports CHARBOUND and STRIPCC together, but the fixed harness has no call or call sequence that reaches their combined boundary-marker behavior. The same behavior was unsupported before the change, so this coverage gap is introduced.
answer.finite_witness: Input bytes 61 c2 90 62 00 (a, U+0090, b, NUL), size 5. A supported utf8proc_map call with CHARBOUND | STRIPCC would retain markers before a and b and remove the marker before the stripped control. The harness accepts these bytes but never makes that call.

scope_contract.reason: Text mapping and UTF-32 normalization are primary harness operations. Their source contracts support the distinct CHARBOUND and STRIPCC options, including the changed combined behavior.

evidence.quote:
/** Strips and/or convers control characters.
   *
   * NLF-sequences are transformed into space, except if one of the
   * NLF2LS/PS/LF options is given. HorizontalTab (HT) and FormFeed (FF)
   * are treated as a NLF-sequence in this case.  All other control
   * characters are simply removed.
   */
  UTF8PROC_STRIPCC   = (1<<9),
  /**
   * Performs unicode case folding, to be able to do a case-insensitive
   * string comparison.
   */
  UTF8PROC_CASEFOLD  = (1<<10),
  /**
   * Inserts 0xFF bytes at the beginning of each sequence which is
   * representing a single grapheme cluster (see UAX#29).
   */
  UTF8PROC_CHARBOUND = (1<<11),

feasible_trigger.reason: The finite, NUL-terminated witness passes the entry guards. The after mapping path can generate boundary sentinels, normalize them with STRIPCC, and encode retained sentinels as markers when both options are supplied.

observable_consequence.reason: The supported result retains markers for surviving text while removing the marker immediately before a stripped control. No old-harness operation reaches that combined behavior.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete harness entry passes STRIPCC only to direct normalization and CHARBOUND only to separate map calls. Every map call consumes the original data and frees its result. The two-step mapping route shown in the added test is therefore absent from this target; the fixed normalization helpers also use other options.

identity_preserved.reason: Both versions are assessed for the same combined marker-retention and control-marker-removal tuple against the same fixed harness. Before, STRIPCC also removed negative markers; after, it preserves them and can remove the marker before a stripped control.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: With CHARBOUND | STRIPCC, retain boundary markers for surviving text and remove the marker before a stripped control.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Map valid UTF-8 text containing a control and surviving characters with CHARBOUND | STRIPCC, or feed a STRIPCC mapping result into a CHARBOUND mapping call.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The harness uses STRIPCC in direct UTF-32 normalization and CHARBOUND in separate map calls; each map call takes the original input.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: The combined retained-text-marker and removed-control-marker result is unreachable through the target.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: The source test demonstrates two-step mapping as an equivalent route, but the harness does not chain mapping results.
